 In Frigid Pipeline, Ukrainians Launched 'Operation Impossible' 
 Service members crawled for weeks underground to thwart Russian advance near Kupiansk 
 By 
 Jenn Gidman 
 with Newser.AI 
 Posted Nov 18, 2026 7:55 AM CST 
 Copied 
 In Frigid Pipeline, Ukrainians Launched 'Operation Impossible' 
 Check out the video.
 (YouTube) 
 Ukrainian troops say one of their latest tactics against Russia involved crawling for miles through a dead gas line. Members of the National Guard's Khartiia Corps claim they spent weeks inside a decommissioned Soviet-era pipeline in the Kharkiv region this fall, moving for 9 miles on wheeled carts and winches through frigid water and lingering natural gas to surface behind Russian positions near the front-line city of Kupiansk, per CBS News . The unit, which dubbed the mission "Operation Veles," describes close combat with grenades and small arms inside the roughly 3-foot-wide pipe and says Russian forces had blocked some sections with obstacles, including corpses. 
 "The Russians had already tried to use underground gas pipelines to move through our positions and launch assault operations. Ukrainian warriors have successfully transformed this tactic, modernized it, and made it much more sophisticated and technologically advanced," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, per the Kyiv Independent , which notes that Zelensky claimed about 100 Russian troops were "eliminated" during the operation and dozens captured. 
 CBS notes it can't independently verify the claims of what UNITED24 calls the "perfect hiding place," though Russian officials have acknowledged a Ukrainian raid. Analysts say the operation—which some troops dubbed "Operation Impossible," per UNITED24 —underscores how drone-packed skies are pushing both armies underground as the war grinds on.
